scope: Independent public source and fake Win32 leaf review of the fixed-path OKX M01 V3 metadata rebinder. No protected deployment contents or private input were read; no Windows API, process, account, provider, native payload, or M01 route was invoked.

review_checks: The actual production _Win32Leaves adapter is exercised against in-memory fake Win32/API leaves. No native Windows function is called.

Fixed deployment metadata opens request GENERIC_READ, GENERIC_WRITE, READ_CONTROL, and READ_ATTRIBUTES with FILE_SHARE_READ and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT. The share mode makes acquisition fail against an existing writer and blocks later write or delete opens while held; read, write, and readback use the same captured handles.

Handle identity is volume plus file index. The pinned private API rejects reparse points and rejects file link counts other than one. ACL checks bind the deployment directory, existing metadata files, backup directory, and backup files to the current SID with the expected protected owner-only DACL.

The fixed backup child is checked for prior existence and created without overwrite. Backup files use CREATE_NEW, zero sharing, owner-only descriptors, flush, and same-handle GENERIC_READ readback before either deployment document is changed.

The old admission is canonical and bound to the fixed old source-map SHA-256 and R1 review reference. The new source map is fixed by its physical 2,877-byte SHA-256, canonical JSON, and exact 19-member map; the new admission binds that physical digest and the R2 review reference.

The transition writes the source map first and the admission second, then rereads and validates both. Any uncertain write, readback, flush, deadline, or close after mutation retains the live handle set in _ORPHANED_CONTEXTS and returns only a finite code plus five booleans.

The superseding test covers backup same-handle readback failure: it maps to protected_write_uncertain, leaves both deployment documents unchanged, and retains the handle context. The full superseding fake suite passed 14 tests.
root_caller_preconditions: Before an actual metadata call, Root must hold the exact 19 public source leases, the exact source-map/review JSON/review README bytes, and the separately held reviewed test bytes for the full call, then verify the source identities again afterward.

Root must supply the exact private custody module from CUv2 and independently bind the supplied current_reader runtime functions and globals to the exact map-pinned source. The helper checks the reader name, origin, constants, and callable presence, but does not itself prove the code/global identity of the supplied reader functions.

Root must establish the fixed target ancestry is stable and appropriate for the protected deployment. The helper checks identities and reparse status for opened ancestors, and owner-only ACLs on the deployment and backup directories/files; it does not verify ACLs on D:/ or D:/temp.

Root must independently verify the fixed backup child is absent before invoking. If any result reports handles_released=false or any mutation/readback state is uncertain, retain the interactive host/context and do not treat the result as accepted metadata state.
limitations: This review authorizes only the Root-controlled protected metadata rebinding step. It does not authorize or claim an account, provider, native API, M01 route, or formal case acceptance.

The protected deployment directory, its files, ACLs, and old-map bytes were not read in this independent review. The old-map digest is checked in source and exercised only with synthetic fake bytes in tests.

The fake suite has a hardlink negative case but no explicit reparse negative test; reparse rejection was confirmed by inspecting the pinned private API path. The fake suite cannot establish actual Windows filesystem or ACL behavior on the host.
